#### 1. atrial fibrillation, familial, 3  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.496)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-5576890, Reactome:R-HSA-5576893)

**Proposed mechanism:** KCNE2 (HGNC:18676) —BINDS→ KCNQ1/KCNE2 potassium channel function (GO:0005400); KCNQ1 (HGNC:6404) —BINDS→ KCNQ1/KCNE2 potassium channel function (GO:0005400); KCNQ1/KCNE2 potassium channel function (GO:0005400) —LEADS_TO→ Cardiac action potential duration (HP:0011679); Cardiac action potential duration (HP:0011679) —LEADS_TO→ Atrial fibrillation (HP:0011679); Cardiac action potential duration (HP:0011679) —LEADS_TO→ Long QT syndrome (HP:0001642). Mutations in KCNE2 and KCNQ1 lead to haploinsufficiency of the KCNQ1/KCNE2 potassium channel. This channel is critical for regulating cardiac action potential duration. Reduced function of this channel prolongs the action potential, which can manifest as Long QT syndrome and predispose to atrial fibrillation.

**How to falsify it:** If mutations in KCNE2 or KCNQ1 are found to cause a gain-of-function effect or are not associated with altered cardiac action potential duration in patient-derived cells or animal models, this hypothesis would be falsified. _(variant: Common variants (AF > 0.01) in known pathogenic regions of KCNE2 and KCNQ1)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared mechanism involving the KCNQ1/KCNE2 channel provides a basis for exploring therapeutic strategies that modulate potassium channel function for both Long QT syndrome and familial atrial fibrillation, potentially leading to combined treatment approaches or improved risk stratification.

#### 2. long QT syndrome 1  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.489)

Mutations in KCNQ1 (causing Disease A) and KCNE2 (causing Disease B) disrupt the function of the KCNQ1/KCNE2 potassium channel complex. This disruption leads to impaired cardiac repolarization (QT interval prolongation), predisposing to arrhythmias, syncope, and in the case of KCNQ1, also seizures. The shared convergence is the compromised function of this specific potassium channel complex.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of a pathogenic variant in either KCNQ1 or KCNE2 with a minor allele frequency > 1% in gnomAD would falsify the claim of these genes being solely responsible for rare, pathogenic variants causing these specific diseases. Furthermore, if experiments demonstrated that KCNQ1 and KCNE2 function in completely independent cellular pathways with no overlap in downstream effectors, this would also falsify the proposed mechanistic link. _(variant: HGNC:6343|HGNC:27979)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared reliance on the KCNQ1/KCNE2 potassium channel complex for preventing both Long QT syndrome 1 and a subset of epilepsy cases offers opportunities for therapeutic strategies that target the common pathway. For instance, drugs aimed at modulating the activity or stability of this channel complex could potentially treat overlapping symptoms across both conditions.
